title: Ole Buddrus from UBS Bar Support Hamburg via the BMGP 2009
description: Posted via email from Joerg Meyer

asr.full_text: Ulle... from UBS. Hi. Three questions... or four if I may? Well done. Hakali Martinik, Grand Prix. What do you do here? We're doing a competition that contains legends, that means every bar man is able to present himself with the facets he knows the best. It's a molecular mix logo, it's a flair bartender, you don't know it. We can all see that at the best of this competition. So what do you do as a company... What part of this do you focus company? what part do you provide here? we do all the competition organizations, most of all we put the computers together and wipe the floor with we want to try to use the toilets maybe you are out crawling from the bottom the floor can be through? that's Action TV, that's ok how many employees do you have at your event? we are two 14 people plus the jury Yes, this is ok, ok how many people work here? We are around fourteen, we also have our jury, which are working at various places, because we're doing the preliminaries at the Cubotel, at the Tape club in the finals. How many days do you have to work at this event? In the preparation? I think that you're working between 12 to 14 days until you're finished, then you usually have one or two days in the actual matches. 2 years ago there was a change of direction with the new Bakati team. How does this whole thing compare to the previous ones? What do you think the difference is from earlier, right now? I think Bacardi noticed that it's not so charming when people keep fighting. Martin Bonprix is one of the few competitions that makes you work together. And it's not the fight between the classics, The Flairers or the Molecular Mixologists anymore but this is about the drink and everyone can use it all. And I think it's what makes this competition special, and that is a partner. I support that, thanks a lot.
